utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-95-13/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Mile Mrksic and Veselin Sljvancanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Let's make sure that the audio equipment is working. Mr. Mrksic, can -- sorry. Mr. Mrksic, can you hear me? THE ACCUSED MRKSIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can hear you very well indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sljivancanin, can you hear me? THE ACCUSED SLJIVANCANIN: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Meron, I can hear you very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I presume the counsel can hear me for Defence and Prosecution, and I would ask for appearances. Prosecution, Ms. Brady is there, I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Helen Brady appearing on behalf of the Prosecution, and with me today, this afternoon, is Mr. Paul Rogers and our case manager, Ms. Alma Imamovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. For Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. Mr. Mrksic is represented by Mr. Miroslav Vasic and Mr. Domazet. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic. Counsel for Mr. Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Novak Lukic and Stephane Bourgon for Mr. Sljivancanin, and with us is our legal assistant, Maja Dokmanovic and Marie-Claude Fournier. I hope that she can remain at this status conference with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: She can. Thank you. As you are aware, Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires that status conferences be held every 120 days for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A status conference serves two primary purposes; first, it allows the appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to their appeal or detention conditions; second, it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. The status conference is also an opportunity for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained persons. The last status conference in this case took place on 16 October 2008. Where both Mr. Mrksic and Mr. Sljivancanin are presently in the custody of the Tribunal, Mr. Sljivancanin's custody is only for the period of the appeals hearing, and he will soon be returning to the provisional release granted to him pursuant to the Appeals Chamber decision of 11 December 2007. I would like to begin the status conference by inquiring into Mr. Mrksic's and Mr. Sljivancanin's health. Mr. Mrksic, anything I should know about your health problems? THE ACCUSED MRKSIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you already know everything. Now I feel all right. I'm not experiencing any problems, and I am satisfied with the treatment I am receiving in the Detention Unit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mrksic. Mr. Sljivancanin. THE ACCUSED SLJIVANCANIN: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Meron, I have no problems to put forward to you today. Thank you once again for allowing me to be on provisional release until the final judgement. I am adhering to all your orders, and that is how I believe things will remain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sljivancanin. You may sit down. Now, on the update of the case, as you all know, the appeals hearing has been completed, and I note that we will decide in due course, soon, on Mr. Mrksic's confidential motions pursuant to Rule 115 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. I further note that we have received Mr. Mrksic's confidential motion for provisional release, and we will be issuing a decision in this matter in due course. At this point, I would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise. Ms. Brady.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: No issues from us, Your Honour, save to say that we'll be filing our response to that confidential request for provisional release. We hope to do so later today and at the latest by Monday. The due date is actually Monday, but we're endeavouring to speed that up, and hopefully we'll be able to do it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you for that, Ms. Brady. Mr. Vasic, anything that you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We are awaiting the decisions Your Honour mentioned. I only wish to say that I have received another set of new documents from my learned friend. I found them in my locker, and I will deal with them after the status conference. I have nothing more to add. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: For Mr. Sljivancanin, Mr. Lukic. Nothing?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Since there are no other matters to be raised, I thank the parties for their attendance and call these proceedings to a close. Thank you very much.
